principles: Closed-set narrow trust for story-dir artifacts stays (B-b9d0); fixes add named entries, never open the set
A recurring manual-catch-up bug class deserves a mechanical invariant, not another one-off patch
Registration is provenance-only; never couple it to gate evidence semantics
Exclusions must be named and auditable, not silent
drivers: Every acceptance-topology story hits a blocking false OUT_OF_SCOPE and needs a manual acknowledge
The registry has needed hand-patching at least twice before (B-12a1, B-3ed9); the class keeps regressing
The scope gate is trust infrastructure in this repo; changes must be minimal and reviewable

options.name: A: register only acceptance-basis.json
cons: three other live acceptance-topology filenames keep triggering the same false violation
regression class stays open; next new artifact repeats the incident

options.name: B: register all four acceptance-topology filenames + coverage-invariant smoke
pros: fixes all live occurrences of the symptom
smoke mechanically derives StoryStore top-level writes and fails with a named filename on any future gap
matches existing lifecycle-registry-contract style of named-divergence checks
cons: smoke needs a named exemption list for the excluded legacy filename

options.name: C: open the classifier to any json under a story dir
cons: reverses the deliberate B-b9d0 narrow-trust policy
arbitrary unknown files under story dirs would silently pass scope

chosen: B: register all four acceptance-topology filenames + coverage-invariant smoke
rationale: B fixes every live occurrence of the false violation and closes the regression class mechanically with a named-divergence invariant, at the cost of a slightly larger but still narrow diff; A leaves known-broken filenames in place and C weakens the trust boundary the scope gate exists to enforce.

preMortem.scenario: The smoke derivation (source scan of store.ts write literals) is too clever and breaks when store.ts is refactored
preMortem.trigger: A rename of writeJson or a move of writers out of store.ts makes the scan return an empty set
preMortem.consequence: The invariant silently passes on zero derived filenames and stops guarding anything
preMortem.mitigation: Assert the derived set has a sane minimum size (>= the count of currently known writers) so an empty or shrunken derivation fails loudly

preMortem.scenario: Registering the four filenames masks a genuine scope violation where an agent hand-edits acceptance-basis.json
preMortem.trigger: A malicious or buggy agent writes arbitrary content to a registered filename in its story dir
preMortem.consequence: The path classifies as lifecycle_artifact and the scope gate does not flag it
preMortem.mitigation: This is unchanged pre-existing semantics for all registered artifacts: classification is provenance-only and content integrity is enforced separately by artifact signatures (acceptance-basis has its own signing per bff1a4c277); no new exposure is added

preMortem.scenario: The named exemption for the legacy receipt-refs filename rots: its write path goes live later and stays unregistered
preMortem.trigger: Future Authority-domain work revives writeLegacyReceiptRefs without touching the registry
preMortem.consequence: That story hits the same false OUT_OF_SCOPE violation this story fixes
preMortem.mitigation: The exemption entry carries a comment naming the owning domain and the condition for removal; the smoke failure message tells the future implementer exactly which constant to update

preMortem.scenario: Parallel in-flight stories (e.g. B-4043 acceptance topology Wave 4) touch the same registry region and conflict on merge
preMortem.trigger: Both stories modify lifecycle-registry.ts near line 599
preMortem.consequence: Merge conflict or combined-state semantic drift at DONE
preMortem.mitigation: The diff is additive set entries only; DONE gate requires merging main first, and the combination review discipline for framework stories covers the merged state
